narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Sixty four times three is one hundred ninety two. Sixty four cubed is one hundred ninety two.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>Cubed means sixty four times sixty four times sixty four, which is far bigger.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The exponent counts copies. It is not a number to multiply by.
removed_beats.on_screen: the hint card leaves; Chintu's bubble shows 64³ = 192; 64 × 64 × 64 is written beside it, far bigger; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='prime'/>To check a split, change every piece back to powers of the same prime.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Then add the exponents, and see that they match the number you started with.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor and the answer card; two check lines appear: change each piece to the same prime; add the exponents and compare

old_misconception.wrong_answer: sixty four cubed is one hundred ninety two
old_misconception.wrong_move: Chintu multiplies sixty four by three and says sixty four cubed is one hundred ninety two. Cubing multiplies sixty four by itself three times, so the bubble is struck.
